cards.title: Configure a local application endpoint
cards.code:
app:
  name: journal
  server:
    host: localhost
    port: 8080
cards.explanation: A complete generic YAML document. server belongs to app; host and port belong to server. YAML validates structure, while an application decides whether these keys are meaningful.

cards.title: List ordered build targets
cards.code:
targets:
  - name: linux
    architectures: [amd64, arm64]
  - name: macos
    architectures: [arm64]
cards.explanation: Two ordered mapping entries, each containing its own architecture sequence. This is YAML data rather than a particular build-system schema.

cards.title: Preserve identifiers while using real booleans
cards.code:
enabled: true
retries: 3
account: "00123"
release_date: "2026-10-15"
mode: "on"
optional: null
cards.explanation: The identifiers, date and mode remain strings across common YAML parser schemas; enabled is boolean and retries is numeric.

cards.title: Keep a message and Windows path intact
cards.code:
message: "Status: ready # verified"
owner: 'Ada''s journal'
path: 'C:\work\journal'
literal: '${HOME}'
cards.explanation: YAML itself does not interpolate environment variables. A consumer such as Compose may interpret dollar expressions later.

cards.title: Store a script and a folded description
cards.code:
script: |
  printf 'one\n'
  printf 'two\n'
description: >-
  Build the local journal
  without external services.
cards.explanation: script ends with a newline and retains two lines. description becomes one sentence with no final newline. Text inside a block is data, not YAML keys.

cards.title: Reuse an ordered list without merge keys
cards.code:
default_regions: &regions
  - eu-west-1
  - ap-southeast-2
preview_regions: *regions
cards.explanation: Both fields resolve to the same two-item list under the generic YAML parser. Do not copy aliases into a CloudFormation template.

cards.title: Run checks for main and pull requests
cards.code:
name: Main checks
"on":
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: printf 'checking\n'
cards.explanation: A complete workflow with filtered pushes, pull requests and a manual trigger. Validation is local; adding this file to .github/workflows enables its triggers.

cards.title: Check out source before listing files
cards.code:
name: Local checks
"on": [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  inspect:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: Inspect source
        run: ls -la
cards.explanation: Checkout makes repository files available to subsequent steps. Action major tags are illustrative; production workflows can pin reviewed commit SHAs.

cards.title: Run a summary after checks pass
cards.code:
name: Local checks
"on": [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: printf 'checked\n'
  summary:
    needs: check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: printf 'all checks passed\n'
cards.explanation: summary runs after check succeeds. It uses a different runner and does not assume files from check exist.

cards.title: Check two Node versions
cards.code:
name: Local checks
"on": [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: [22, 24]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
      - run: node --version
cards.explanation: Expands to two jobs and prints the selected runtime in each. It needs no application dependencies.

cards.title: Print a pull request title through an environment variable
cards.code:
name: Local checks
"on": [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  title:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: printf '%s\n' "$PR_TITLE"
cards.explanation: The event title enters the shell as data through a quoted environment expansion, avoiding expression substitution into shell source.

cards.title: Use a secret only in a manually triggered step
cards.code:
name: Secret presence
"on": workflow_dispatch
permissions: {}
jobs:
  inspect:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEMO_API_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$API_TOKEN" ]; then
            printf 'No demo token configured\n'
          else
            printf 'Demo token is configured\n'
          fi
cards.explanation: Checks presence without printing or using the token. The playground validates the workflow without accessing secrets.

cards.title: Inspect the checkout with a read-only token
cards.code:
name: Local checks
"on": [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  inspect:
    permissions:
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - run: git status --short
cards.explanation: Both the workflow and inspect job request contents read only. No publishing or deployment permissions are granted.

cards.title: Cache npm downloads by the lockfile
cards.code:
name: Local checks
"on": [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
cards.explanation: Requires a committed package-lock.json and test script in the target repository. setup-node caches npm downloads, not node_modules. Local validation checks schema only and does not run these commands.

cards.title: Transfer a generated report to a dependent job
cards.code:
name: Local checks
"on": [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: printf 'ok\n' > report.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: local-report
          path: report.txt
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7
  inspect:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: local-report
      - run: cat report.txt
cards.explanation: needs orders jobs and the upload/download pair transfers report.txt. The playground only validates; no artifact is created remotely.

cards.title: Constrain a queue visibility timeout
cards.code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: Local learning template; validate without deploying
Parameters:
  VisibilitySeconds:
    Type: Number
    Default: 30
    MinValue: 0
    MaxValue: 43200
Resources:
  WorkQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      VisibilityTimeout: !Ref VisibilitySeconds
cards.explanation: A Number input drives an SQS property through Ref. cfn-lint checks the template locally; this snippet does not create a queue.

cards.title: Describe an encrypted work queue
cards.code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: Local learning template; validate without deploying
Resources:
  WorkQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      SqsManagedSseEnabled: true
      MessageRetentionPeriod: 86400
cards.explanation: Describes a queue retaining messages for one day with SQS-managed encryption. Validate locally; deployment would create a billable AWS resource.

cards.title: Expose a queue URL, ARN and stack label
cards.code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: Local learning template; validate without deploying
Resources:
  WorkQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
Outputs:
  QueueUrl:
    Value: !Ref WorkQueue
  QueueArn:
    Value: !GetAtt WorkQueue.Arn
  Label:
    Value: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-worker"
cards.explanation: For AWS::SQS::Queue, Ref yields its URL and GetAtt Arn yields its ARN. Sub expands the stack-name pseudo parameter at deployment, not during ordinary YAML parsing.

cards.title: Choose queue retention by environment
cards.code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: Local learning template; validate without deploying
Parameters:
  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    AllowedValues: [dev, prod]
Conditions:
  IsProduction: !Equals [!Ref Environment, prod]
Resources:
  WorkQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      MessageRetentionPeriod: !If [IsProduction, 1209600, 86400]
cards.explanation: Production retains messages for fourteen days; development for one day. cfn-lint checks both branches without an AWS account.

cards.title: Export a queue ARN with a stack-qualified name
cards.code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: Local learning template; validate without deploying
Resources:
  WorkQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
Outputs:
  WorkerQueueArn:
    Description: ARN for consumers in the same account and Region
    Value: !GetAtt WorkQueue.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-queue-arn"
cards.explanation: A stack-qualified export avoids hard-coding a shared name. No stack or export is created by the local validator.

cards.title: Describe a loopback-only web server
cards.code:
services:
  web:
    image: nginx:1.28-alpine
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:80"
cards.explanation: docker compose config validates this without pulling an image or starting a container. Running it later would expose nginx on localhost port 8080.

cards.title: Keep Redis data in a named volume
cards.code:
services:
  cache:
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
    command: [redis-server, --appendonly, "yes"]
    volumes:
      - cache-data:/data
volumes:
  cache-data:
cards.explanation: The /data directory uses a named volume rather than the container writable layer. config creates neither containers nor volumes.

cards.title: Describe an isolated Redis service network
cards.code:
services:
  cache:
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
    networks: [backend]
networks:
  backend:
    internal: true
cards.explanation: cache joins backend, whose internal flag isolates external connectivity. No host port is published.

cards.title: Give a service a configurable application label
cards.code:
services:
  app:
    image: alpine:3.22
    command: [sh, -c, 'printf "%s\n" "$$APP_LABEL"']
    environment:
      APP_LABEL: "${DEMO_LABEL:-journal}"
      FEATURE_ENABLED: "true"
cards.explanation: Compose uses journal unless DEMO_LABEL is set. The escaped dollar delays APP_LABEL expansion until the container shell. Values shown here are not secrets.

cards.title: Wait for Redis before sending a ping
cards.code:
services:
  cache:
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
    healthcheck:
      test: [CMD, redis-cli, ping]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
  probe:
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
    depends_on:
      cache:
        condition: service_healthy
    command: [redis-cli, -h, cache, ping]
cards.explanation: probe waits for cache health and uses Compose service DNS. Schema validation does not execute the health check or prove runtime availability.

cards.title: Preserve scalar-looking account labels with explicit string tags
cards.code:
account: !!str 00123
feature: !!str false
missing_label: !!str null
retries: !!int "3"
cards.explanation: Complete generic YAML 1.2 document; ruamel.yaml safe loading preserves all three labels as strings and constructs retries as an integer. It needs no custom tag constructors. A downstream application must still validate its own fields.

cards.title: Distinguish a null value from an empty text label
cards.code:
optional: !!null null
empty_label: !!str ""
ratio: !!float "1.5"
enabled: !!bool false
cards.explanation: Generic YAML 1.2 with standard tags only. Null means absent data, while the empty string is present text; false is a boolean and ratio is numeric. Do not use Python-object or arbitrary application tags with a safe loader.

cards.title: Read two ordered environment records from one YAML stream
cards.code:
---
name: dev
replicas: 1
...
---
name: test
replicas: 2
...
cards.explanation: A generic stream for a loader using list(YAML(typ="safe").load_all(text)). It yields two mappings in source order. No application merge occurs; explicitly select a record rather than assuming the second overrides the first.

cards.title: Preserve an intentional empty document between batch records
cards.code:
---
items: []
---
# An empty slot is retained as null.
---
items: [journal]
...
cards.explanation: Generic YAML 1.2 stream, not a workflow or Compose file. load_all returns a mapping, null, then a mapping. A batch importer must choose whether to reject or skip the empty slot; the parser does not silently discard it.

cards.title: Override a timeout while sharing connection defaults
cards.code:
defaults: &defaults
  host: localhost
  timeout: 5
worker:
  <<: *defaults
  timeout: 0
cards.explanation: Generic config requiring a merge-aware reader such as pinned ruamel.yaml; timeout zero is an explicit override, not a missing value. worker inherits host and uses timeout 0. This is a shallow mapping merge, unsuitable for Actions or CloudFormation.

cards.title: Replace a nested option mapping without inheriting its fields
cards.code:
defaults: &defaults
  options:
    retries: 3
    mode: safe
worker:
  <<: *defaults
  options:
    retries: 0
cards.explanation: Merge-aware generic YAML. worker.options replaces the whole inherited options node; mode is absent, not deep-merged. Use explicit nested anchors if deep reuse is needed, and verify your application supports merges before copying.

cards.title: Represent regional ports without duplicate mapping keys
cards.code:
ports:
  west: 8080
  east: 8081
cards.explanation: A complete repaired config for a strict safe loader. Unique region keys preserve both ports. Repeating west loses intent and is rejected by the playground; fix the key rather than disabling duplicate detection.

cards.title: Replace a custom tagged endpoint with portable data
cards.code:
endpoint:
  scheme: http
  host: localhost
  port: 8080
  options: []
cards.explanation: A generic YAML 1.2 mapping needs no custom constructors. An application can validate these explicit fields after parsing. The local checks reject an unsupported !endpoint tag, an indentation tab and an unfinished flow list, then reparse this repaired document.

cards.title: Keep legacy boolean-looking and numeric identifiers as text
cards.code:
labels: ["on", "off", "yes", "no", "012", "2026-10-17", "null"]
empty: ""
absent: ~
zero: 0
cards.explanation: Generic YAML 1.2; all quoted labels remain strings under both pinned 1.1 and 1.2 resolution. ~ is null; empty text and numeric zero remain distinct. ruamel.yaml also resolves dates as timestamps, so quote date labels for portability.

cards.title: Keep glob patterns and a colon-space label literal
cards.code:
include: "*.yaml"
label: "Status: ready # local"
quote: 'it''s ready'
line: "first\nsecond"
cards.explanation: Generic YAML 1.2 document. A leading * would start an alias if unquoted. Single quotes double an apostrophe; double quotes decode the newline escape. YAML quoting does not stop Compose dollar interpolation.

cards.title: Choose strip, clip and keep for notification text
cards.code:
strip: >-
  Build complete
  for journal.

clip: |
  one
  two

keep: |+
  one
  two
cards.explanation: Generic YAML 1.2. strip folds to one line with no final newline; clip retains one final newline; keep preserves the trailing empty line. Copy the complete text including its final blank line; the playground asserts exact strings.

cards.title: Preserve a leading-space line and a paragraph break
cards.code:
indented: |2-
    heading
  body
paragraph: >-
  First paragraph.

  Second paragraph.
    code line
cards.explanation: Generic YAML 1.2. The explicit indentation indicator 2 removes two spaces, so heading retains two spaces and body retains none. A blank line creates a folded paragraph break; more-indented text keeps its line break. This is text storage, not script execution.

cards.title: Share a mapping node while keeping a separate mapping independent
cards.code:
original: &settings
  retries: 3
shared: *settings
independent:
  retries: 3
cards.explanation: Generic YAML 1.2 using ruamel.yaml 0.18.16. original and shared refer to the same loaded mapping; independent has equal values but its own identity. Mutating a loaded alias can affect both names; make a deep copy in application code if isolation is required.

cards.title: Expose a normalized label from a reusable workflow
cards.code:
name: Reusable label
"on":
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      label:
        type: string
        required: true
    outputs:
      label:
        description: Produced label
        value: ${{ jobs.label.outputs.label }}
permissions: {}
jobs:
  label:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      label: ${{ steps.emit.outputs.label }}
    steps:
      - id: emit
        env:
          LABEL: ${{ inputs.label }}
        run: printf 'label=%s\n' "$LABEL" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
cards.explanation: Save as .github/workflows/label.yml. A caller uses jobs.call.uses: ./.github/workflows/label.yml with a single-line string label, then needs.call.outputs.label. The local validator creates that caller and checks its contract. It never evaluates the expression or runs the shell step.

cards.title: Pass a typed count and expose a report output
cards.code:
name: Reusable count
"on":
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      count:
        type: number
        default: 0
    outputs:
      count:
        description: Requested count
        value: ${{ jobs.report.outputs.count }}
permissions: {}
jobs:
  report:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      count: ${{ steps.emit.outputs.count }}
    steps:
      - id: emit
        env:
          COUNT: ${{ inputs.count }}
        run: printf 'count=%s\n' "$COUNT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
cards.explanation: Save as .github/workflows/count.yml and call at job level. count is a numeric input with zero as the default; workflow outputs are strings. actionlint inspects a local caller with omitted/zero values and rejects a string where a number is required. No workflow runs offline.

cards.title: Return a greeting from a local composite action
cards.code:
name: Greeting
description: Return a single-line greeting
inputs:
  name:
    description: Single-line recipient name
    required: true
outputs:
  greeting:
    description: Greeting text
    value: ${{ steps.emit.outputs.greeting }}
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - id: emit
      shell: bash
      env:
        PERSON: ${{ inputs.name }}
      run: |
        test -n "$PERSON" || { printf 'name is required\n' >&2; exit 1; }
        printf 'greeting=Hello %s\n' "$PERSON" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
cards.explanation: Save as .github/actions/greeting/action.yml; checkout before a workflow step uses this directory and with.name. Accept a single-line name; the action checks for empty text explicitly. A later step reads steps.<id>.outputs.greeting. Expressions and shell remain literal fixtures during validation.

cards.title: Append a fixed heading to the runner job summary
cards.code:
name: Summary
description: Append a plain summary line
inputs:
  message:
    description: Summary text
    default: No items
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        MESSAGE: ${{ inputs.message }}
      run: printf '%s\n' "$MESSAGE" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
cards.explanation: Save as .github/actions/summary/action.yml and use it after checkout. Omitted message defaults to No items; an explicitly empty string stays empty. This action appends a summary and has no outputs. Offline validation checks the local input contract; it does not write a runner summary.

cards.title: Cancel stale checks for the same workflow and branch
cards.code:
name: Branch checks
"on": workflow_dispatch
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: printf 'checked\n'
cards.explanation: Complete workflow. The group includes both workflow and ref so concurrent branches do not share the same key. New runs cancel running checks in that group; local tests assert literal expressions and lint valid/invalid contexts, without claiming scheduler execution.

cards.title: Serialize a report job without cancelling the running report
cards.code:
name: Report
"on": workflow_dispatch
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  report:
    concurrency:
      group: report-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: printf 'report\n'
cards.explanation: Complete workflow with job-level concurrency. false preserves the running job, but newer pending jobs can still replace earlier pending jobs; this is not a FIFO queue. The validator checks the configuration without scheduling any report.

cards.title: Describe a summary that survives a failed dependency
cards.code:
name: Summary
"on": workflow_dispatch
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: printf 'checked\n'
  summary:
    needs: check
    if: ${{ always() && !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          RESULT: ${{ needs.check.result }}
        run: printf '%s\n' "$RESULT"
cards.explanation: Complete workflow. The status function removes the implicit success-only gate, while !cancelled() respects cancellation. RESULT remains a literal runner expression in offline checks; do not interpret local lint success as a failed-job execution test.

cards.title: Gate a follow-up on a specific dependency result
cards.code:
name: Follow-up
"on": workflow_dispatch
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: printf 'checked\n'
  followup:
    needs: check
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.check.result == 'success' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: printf 'ready\n'
cards.explanation: Complete workflow checking only the direct check dependency. Quoted expression syntax keeps leading ! from becoming a YAML tag. A skipped/failed dependency does not meet success; offline validation checks references and literal structure only.

cards.title: Select queue retention from an environment table
cards.code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Parameters:
  Stage:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    AllowedValues: [dev, prod]
Mappings:
  Retention:
    dev:
      Seconds: "86400"
    prod:
      Seconds: "1209600"
Resources:
  WorkQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      MessageRetentionPeriod: !FindInMap [Retention, !Ref Stage, Seconds]
cards.explanation: Complete non-deployed template. Stage is restricted to table keys; FindInMap selects a numeric property from literal strings accepted by CloudFormation. cfn-lint checks the lookup shape and resource schema offline; it does not resolve a live stack.

cards.title: Read a fixed regional label into an output
cards.code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Mappings:
  Labels:
    west:
      Name: journal-west
    east:
      Name: journal-east
Resources:
  WorkQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
Outputs:
  RegionLabel:
    Value: !FindInMap [Labels, west, Name]
cards.explanation: Complete template using an explicit fixed lookup rather than a runtime region. No transform is required. Local lint rejects missing mapping names and wrong argument counts; tests assert both table entries and the exact intrinsic tree.

cards.title: Route repeatedly failed messages to a dead-letter queue
cards.code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Resources:
  DeadLetters:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
  WorkQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      RedrivePolicy:
        deadLetterTargetArn: !GetAtt DeadLetters.Arn
        maxReceiveCount: 5
cards.explanation: Complete local template, never deployed. The nested policy refers to a queue in the same template; maxReceiveCount is positive. cfn-lint checks its shape and GetAtt reference. Message movement is a runtime AWS behavior outside this fixture.

cards.title: Attach two structured tags to an encrypted queue
cards.code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Resources:
  WorkQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      SqsManagedSseEnabled: true
      Tags:
        - Key: application
          Value: journal
        - Key: owner
          Value: local-learning
cards.explanation: Complete template. Tags is an ordered list of mappings, not a mapping of names to values; boolean encryption is independent of the tags. The validator rejects scalar Tags and unknown properties without any AWS call.

cards.title: Join a parameter and queue name into a display label
cards.code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Parameters:
  Prefix:
    Type: String
    Default: journal
Resources:
  WorkQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
Outputs:
  Label:
    Value:
      Fn::Join:
        - ":"
        - - !Ref Prefix
          - worker
cards.explanation: Complete template with long-form Join and a nested Ref. The delimiter is literal text and the second argument is a sequence. cfn-lint checks types; the local parser asserts the intrinsic structure, without claiming to resolve Ref.

cards.title: Substitute a mapped resource ARN into a local description
cards.code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Resources:
  WorkQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
Outputs:
  Description:
    Value:
      Fn::Sub:
        - "Queue ${QueueArn}"
        - QueueArn:
            Fn::GetAtt: [WorkQueue, Arn]
cards.explanation: Complete template. Long-form Sub supplies QueueArn through a variable mapping containing GetAtt. This avoids stacking short tags and documents the exact two-element argument list. Linting rejects undefined variables; no ARN is fetched.

cards.title: Describe a tiny image with an inline Dockerfile
cards.code:
services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile_inline: |
        FROM alpine:3.22
        CMD ["printf", "journal\n"]
cards.explanation: Complete Compose config for 5.5.1. Inline Dockerfile avoids needing a companion file for config validation. The validator preserves the literal Dockerfile and resolves context; it never builds, pulls Alpine, or checks Dockerfile instructions.

cards.title: Describe a build-time label with an explicit default argument
cards.code:
services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      args:
        APP_LABEL: "${DEMO_LABEL:-journal}"
      dockerfile_inline: |
        FROM alpine:3.22
        ARG APP_LABEL
        LABEL app.label=$$APP_LABEL
cards.explanation: Compose 5.5.1. Compose expands DEMO_LABEL in args, while $APP_LABEL in the block is escaped below for the image build stage. Build args are public configuration, not a place for credentials. config validation does not execute a build.

cards.title: Keep a debug toolbox optional beside the cache
cards.code:
services:
  cache:
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
  toolbox:
    image: alpine:3.22
    profiles: [debug]
    command: [printf, "local debug\n"]
cards.explanation: Complete Compose 5.5.1 document. Default config contains cache; --profile debug also includes toolbox. The local validator asserts both selections and leaves all containers stopped. This card has no override file requirement.

cards.title: Enable an isolated test runner only for the test profile
cards.code:
services:
  cache:
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
  test:
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
    profiles: [test]
    depends_on:
      cache:
        condition: service_started
    command: [redis-cli, -h, cache, ping]
cards.explanation: Complete Compose 5.5.1 config. --profile test selects the runner and its always-enabled cache dependency. service_started checks startup order, not readiness; use a health check for readiness. config inspects the selection without issuing a Redis request.

cards.title: Override a mode and add an optional inspector
cards.code:
services:
  app:
    environment:
      MODE: local
  inspector:
    image: alpine:3.22
    profiles: [debug]
    command: [printf, "inspect\n"]
cards.explanation: Override fragment for Compose 5.5.1. Supply playground/yaml/depth/compose.base.yaml first, then this file with -f; that base declares app.image and KEEP=yes. MODE becomes local while KEEP remains. --profile debug enables inspector. The fragment is not a standalone service definition.

cards.title: Replace published ports and clear an inherited environment field
cards.code:
services:
  app:
    ports: !override
      - "127.0.0.1:9090:80"
    environment:
      MODE: !reset null
cards.explanation: Compose 5.5.1 override fragment; use playground/yaml/depth/compose.base.yaml first. !override replaces the base port list, while !reset removes MODE and preserves KEEP. A generic safe YAML loader rejects these tags; Compose handles them. Validation needs no daemon.

cards.title: Require a nonempty external label but preserve a runtime dollar
cards.code:
services:
  app:
    image: alpine:3.22
    environment:
      APP_LABEL: "${DEMO_LABEL:?Set a nonempty DEMO_LABEL}"
    command: [sh, -c, 'printf "%s\n" "$$APP_LABEL"']
cards.explanation: Compose 5.5.1 complete config. DEMO_LABEL must be set and nonempty; config fails with the supplied message otherwise. $$ defers APP_LABEL expansion to the container shell. This local fixture supplies only a dummy label and never starts a container.

cards.title: Wait for a one-shot preparation job rather than a health probe
cards.code:
services:
  prepare:
    image: alpine:3.22
    command: [printf, "prepared\n"]
  app:
    image: alpine:3.22
    depends_on:
      prepare:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    command: [printf, "ready\n"]
cards.explanation: Compose 5.5.1 complete config. A one-shot dependency must finish successfully; this differs from service_started and service_healthy. config validates the dependency contract but cannot assert a process exit status without running containers.
